messages:
alejandro: Heads-up — PR #842 (docs: retry/caching behavior) is ready for final review but I'm blocked on two runtime clarifications before we can merge. CI preview link is up but I don't want to ship potentially misleading behavior notes.

docs-bot: Preview: https://docs-preview.redwood.internal/pr-842 — status: failed (linkcheck).

alejandro: The linkcheck failure is due to a runtime doc link that points to an older API page; I'll fix that. Main blockers are: (1) exact behavior for 429 / rate-limit retries and (2) how streaming requests interact with SDK-level retry.

maya: Quick Q: when we say "no retry on 4xx" in the current draft, does that explicitly exclude 429? org expects 429 to be optionally retryable. Also streaming + retry is fuzzy in the text — need concrete wording.

kevin: Short answer: 429 is treated as rate-limit and controlled by retry_on_rate_limit flag. The older sentence "no retry on 4xx" is too broad — we should say "no automatic retry on non-rate-limit 4xx (e.g., 400/403). 429 is controlled separately." 

kevin: For streaming: our SDK will NOT automatically re-stream partial responses. If streaming=true and an error happens mid-stream that is retryable, the SDK surface is an error. Only non-streaming requests are retried automatically. We should document this explicitly.

maya: That matches what I thought. Can we add a small example to make it obvious?

alejandro: Proposed snippet in docs (feel free to refine):
```js
// non-streaming -> SDK will retry up to max_retries on 429 if retry_on_rate_limit=true
client.request({
  model: "redwood-base:1.0",
  prompt: "...",
  retry_on_rate_limit: true,
  max_retries: 2,
  streaming: false
});

// streaming -> SDK will NOT retry automatically; app should handle partial-state or restart
client.request({ streaming: true /* no automatic retry */ });
```

kevin: That's good. Add a line that recommends apps set idempotency keys for long-running non-streaming ops they expect to retry.

maya: Next: cache behavior. The draft currently says "cache key defaults to model + prompt". Is that always true? What about calls with function-calling or structured outputs?

chris: Runtime note: default cache key includes model, prompt, model_args (temperature/stop), and a hash of the request body. Function-call arguments are part of the body hash, so they are included. However, we exclude transient fields (client-side request_id, timestamps). If folks set cache_key:null we disable caching. Worth documenting examples where function-calls may produce nondeterministic outputs and recommending disabling cache.

maya: Can you add that as a short bullet with example? e.g., "If your prompt includes nondeterministic elements (timestamps, random tokens) set cache_key: null"

chris: Also one more runtime edge: automatic model fallback (smart-routing) — is the docs line "we auto-fallback to smaller variants" accurate? That could be misleading for Dedicated/Private setups.

sre-jen: Yes — ops asked that earlier. We need to call out when fallback is allowed (hosted only, and only if enable_fallback is true at request or project level). Otherwise the request fails and SLOs trigger.

chris: Correct. Clarify: smart-routing fallback is OFF by default for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can opt-in with enable_fallback: true; runtime will try compatible quantized variants when capacity or latency triggers the policy. Add sample config:
```json
{ "enable_fallback": true, "fallback_policy": "latency-first" }
```

alejandro: Perfect. Action items:
- kevin: update the retry/streaming paragraph and add the idempotency recommendation (small change).
- chris: add explicit cache_key default explanation and example about function-calls + nondeterminism.
- me (alejandro): fix linkcheck and re-run preview.

maya: Once those go in I'll do a final pass. If CI passes I'm happy to approve.

docs-bot: CI re-run queued for PR #842 (preview link will refresh once checks complete).

alejandro: Thanks all — will push updates within the hour. Please ping in-thread if you notice any other gotchas. :pray:
